title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (1) must be W = mgh - (1/2)mu^2 or an equivalent algebraic form.

title: Terminal velocity derivation
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (2) must correctly express v_m in terms of r, yielding v_m = sqrt((4πρgr)/(3k)) or an equivalent form.

title: Force balance at terminal velocity
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must set the gravitational force (mg) equal to the given air resistance force (kr^2 v_m^2) at terminal velocity.

title: Mass from density and volume
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must correctly relate the raindrop's mass m to its density ρ and spherical volume (V = (4/3)πr^3).

title: Impulse-momentum setup for disk
description: Important: For part (3), the solution must apply the impulse-momentum theorem correctly to molecules above and below the disk, considering relative velocities.

title: Air resistance proportional to v^2
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (3) must show f is proportional to v^2, specifically deriving a form like f = 2Sv^2 n m_0.

title: Incorrect work-energy sign
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the work done against air resistance is written as (1/2)mu^2 - mgh, reversing the sign.

title: Algebraic error in exponent
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the terminal velocity expression incorrectly handles the exponent from the force balance (e.g., writing v_m proportional to r instead of sqrt(r)).

title: Missing volume or mass step
description: Pitfall: Penalize if part (2) jumps directly to the answer without substituting m = ρ*(4/3πr^3) into the force balance.

title: Unit or proportionality check
description: Optional: Award credit if the student explicitly checks or comments on the units/dimensions of the derived expressions for consistency.
